From AI factories and AI agents to robotics and healthcare, Jensen took the stage at #NVIDIAGTC Berlin to show how AI is taking shape across the continent.

Here's a look back at the highlights: https://t.co/8nJReDvmH7

After a breast cancer diagnosis, one of the hardest questions is whether it will come back.

@SimBioSys is helping doctors and patients better understand that risk. Powered by NVIDIA technology, its FDA-cleared TumorSight Risk analyzes an existing breast MRI alongside pathology and clinical information to estimate the risk of cancer returning at five and ten years.

For women with HR-positive, HER2-negative early-stage breast cancer, those insights can be available before surgery, giving them and their doctors more information as they talk through treatment options.

AI can help give patients and their doctors more information when the decisions ahead feel most difficult.

I built 𝚌𝚙𝚞-𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚝, a reproduction of @openai's findings of covert communication using the CPU.

It runs on a generic host with 2+ Firecracker microVMs with no internet access. Works on x86 and even my M5 chip.

I was able to chat via 3 separate mechanisms:
① CPU contention
② Cache eviction timing
③ DRAM bandwidth contention 

… across multiple CPUs, defeating all Firecracker's production recommendations (no SMT, no KSM, tenants pinned to different cores.)

Essentially, if shared hardware is involved, there's a good chance your agents can communicate covertly. And with really decent latency.

The good news: this is decidedly different from a *side-channel attack* where the agents could steal information (Meltdown/Spectre), a category of attack that providers like Vercel Sandbox mitigate. Further, in our real-world environment, these 'whispering' techniques are much harder to pull off and easier for us to monitor and detect (sampling hardware counters + lots of at-scale statistical data.)

Noteworthy: ironically, OpenAI and Anthropic's models refused to do this work. Open weight models got the job done. I'm worried the labs' stance might backfire and get in the way of helping developers build correct and secure systems. e.g: building a secure sandbox requires having this kind of analysis, and without it, we'll have a less secure world.

Yes. Different cores, no SMT involvement, no KSM/dedup, no shared pages. Only  requirement is two cooperating agents in same machine.

cpuset can partition cores, but it cannot partition the memory pipe (DRAM channels and the memory controller are one socket entity in this machine, but I think socket pinning could mitigate)

Btw, there are even more whispering attacks available, and there's plenty of literature to cram through.
@johncodes @OpenAI With two-socket boxes, you just need 3 covert tenants and they can still communicate

For centuries, the architecture of the firm has barely changed: hierarchies of people organized into departments and coordinated through bureaucracy.

AI agents are about to upend that.

We’re moving toward the self-driving company where humans exercise judgment and agents execute most of the work.

At Replit, we’re building the foundation for this new kind of company. We’re calling it “the Agent Habitat.”

Marc Andreessen wrote a fantastic piece placing this shift in the history of computing. Every major computing revolution began with chaos before businesses figured out how to harness it.

OpenAI asked three scientific communities how to release its discoveries and got three different answers:

Mathematicians: “Just post it. Who gives a shit anymore.”

Computer scientists: “Open source it, but also pay for our conference.”

Physicists: “Leave it to us, nerds.” https://t.co/5cpEOIADpY
